- When sentiment is strongly positive (e.g., >0.30) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peak by 5–10%.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.30), model underestimates; adjust upward by 5–10% to avoid missing upside momentum.
- Model consistently overreacts to short-term spikes; apply a 1–2 day lag correction to avoid overshoot after price surges.
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is >10% above recent 7-day average, reduce by 2–5% unless sentiment supports continuation.
- For 30-day horizon, model often fails to capture late-stage momentum; add 1–3% upward adjustment in final 5–7 days if sentiment remains positive.
- If sentiment turns from negative to positive over 3–5 days, model lags in recognizing shift; adjust forecast upward by 3–7% in next 3–5 days.
